title: Power Apps: Card gallery, Persona, Avatar group and Metrics card canvas controls reach general availability
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, maker setting, preview qualifications and licensing statements are supported. Add a citation for the explanation that Persona's default formulas display the signed-in user's details.

claims.where: title; What's changing; changes
claims.claim: The roadmap plans general availability for Card gallery, Persona, Avatar group and Metrics card.
claims.quote:
The following controls for canvas apps are reaching general availability:

•	Card gallery

•	Persona

•	Avatar group

•	Metrics card

claims.quote: These controls provide reusable patterns for responsive record cards, individual and grouped identities, and key metrics.

claims.claim: Makers supply data, presence values and metric calculations through properties and Power Fx.
claims.quote: Makers supply data, presence values, and metric calculations through properties and Power Fx.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The modern controls reference labels Persona as preview but does not label the other three as preview.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: These are maker-authored canvas app controls used in Power Apps Studio.
claims.quote: You can also provide feedback for individual controls in the Power Apps Studio from the control properties

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: For an app open for editing, the maker enables Modern controls and themes under Settings > Updates > New.
claims.quote: With your canvas app open for editing: 1. On the command bar, select Settings > Updates. 2. Select the New tab and then turn on Modern controls and themes.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: No API or automation equivalent for the app's Modern controls and themes setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps modern controls and themes enable setting PowerShell Set-AdminPowerApp Power Platform API pac admin automation; modern controls Power Platform API pac PowerShell. Read overview, PowerShell support and pac admin excerpts; no equivalent found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The general modern controls setting is not documented as an individual switch for each of the four controls.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps Card gallery Persona Avatar group Metrics card admin disable controls tenant rollout role licensing; modern controls disable tenant canvas. Read overview, all four control pages and Tenant settings; no individual switch found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The capability is maker-opt-in: makers choose whether to enable and use modern controls in their apps.
claims.quote: Select the New tab and then turn on Modern controls and themes. The app refreshes with the new app authoring menu. Modern controls are part of existing categories.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified a rollout mechanism or automatic insertion of these controls into existing apps.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps Card gallery Persona Avatar group Metrics card existing apps automatically rollout licensing meter; Power Apps Card gallery Persona Avatar group Metrics card admin disable controls tenant rollout role licensing. Read all four control pages and overview; no such statement found.

claims.where: summary; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No administrator action or administrator-level switch specific to these four controls is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps Card gallery Persona Avatar group Metrics card admin disable controls tenant rollout role licensing; modern controls disable tenant canvas. Read Tenant settings, overview and the four control pages; no feature-specific administrator switch or action found.

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: No additional required role for these four controls is stated beyond their Learn documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps Card gallery Persona Avatar group Metrics card admin disable controls tenant rollout role licensing; Avatar group Metrics card license pricing meter role rollout. Read all four control pages; no control-specific role prerequisite found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Persona's Name defaults to User().FullName.
claims.quote: Name – The primary text line and the name used to derive avatar initials. The default is User().FullName.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Persona's Caption defaults to User().Email.
claims.quote: Caption – The secondary text line. The default is User().Email.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Persona's Image defaults to User().Image.
claims.quote: Image – The image displayed in the avatar. The default is User().Image. When the image is blank or unavailable, the avatar displays initials derived from Name.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Persona's presence is formula-driven rather than retrieved live by the control from Teams or Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Presence and OutOfOffice are formula-driven display values. The control doesn't retrieve live presence from Microsoft Teams or Microsoft Graph.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Avatar group's presence reflects supplied values rather than a live connection established by the control.
claims.quote: Presence reflects the values your app supplies; the control doesn't establish a live presence connection.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Card gallery displays the table provided through Items and maker-defined content mappings.
claims.quote: Items | Table of records to display. Use a data source, collection, or inline Table() expression.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Avatar group displays the table provided through Items and mapped per-item properties.
claims.quote: Bind Items to a table, then map its columns with the ItemName, ItemImage, and other per-item properties.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Metrics card's main value is the text supplied through DisplayText.
claims.quote: DisplayText | Text displayed as the main metric. Format numbers or dates with Power Fx before displaying them

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Metrics card does not aggregate records; makers calculate the metric.
claims.quote: The card displays the values you provide. It doesn't calculate an aggregate, compare periods, or infer whether a change is favorable. Use Power Fx formulas to calculate your metric and set its presentation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Card gallery uses a fixed shared card height.
claims.quote: All cards share CardHeight. Per-record automatic height isn't available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Card gallery exposes no built-in search property.
claims.quote: The control doesn't expose built-in search and sorting properties. Prepare the table supplied to Items with appropriate Power Fx formulas.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Card gallery exposes no built-in sorting property.
claims.quote: The control doesn't expose built-in search and sorting properties. Prepare the table supplied to Items with appropriate Power Fx formulas.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Card gallery virtualisation does not guarantee delegation or complete retrieval of the data source.
claims.quote: Virtualization reduces the number of rendered cards; it doesn't guarantee that a data-source formula delegates or retrieves every record. Check the delegation behavior of your data source and formulas.

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: Persona has no Studio upgrade action from another control, so adoption in an existing app requires manual authoring.
claims.quote: Persona is a new control. Studio doesn't offer an upgrade action from another control.

claims.claim: No meter specific to these controls is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps Card gallery Persona Avatar group Metrics card existing apps automatically rollout licensing meter; Avatar group Metrics card license pricing meter role rollout. Read all four control pages and the pay-as-you-go meter overview and Power Apps section; no control-specific meter found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The roadmap item states no licensing requirement.
claims.quote: These controls provide reusable patterns for responsive record cards, individual and grouped identities, and key metrics. Makers supply data, presence values, and metric calculations through properties and Power Fx.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Apps using premium connectors need an appropriate Power Apps entitlement.
claims.quote: End users need an entitlement to access a premium app. Some examples of features that require premium entitlements include: premium connectors

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Power Apps per-app pay-as-you-go meter supports app access without a standalone Power Apps licence.
claims.quote: The Power Apps per-app meter enables users to use any type of app without needing to have a Power Apps license. The Power Apps per-app meter provides access to both canvas, and model-driven apps for authenticated users.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Binding a control to a premium connector leaves the containing app subject to premium-app entitlement requirements.
claims.quote: What capabilities make my app require a premium license? Some examples of features that require premium entitlements include: premium connectors

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The containing canvas app's data connections and resource-sharing permissions govern access to the data displayed by these controls.
claims.quote: Some connections (such as SQL Server with SQL or Windows authentication) are implicitly shared with the app when you share the app with other users. Other connections require users to create their own connections and explictly grant security privileges

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Metrics card supports maker-written OnSelect actions.
claims.quote: OnSelect – Action that runs when a user activates the card. The card becomes an activation target when this property has a formula and DisplayMode is DisplayMode.Edit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Persona's default User() formulas refer to the user signed in to the canvas app.
claims.quote: In Power Apps, show the full name, the email address, and the picture that's associated with the user who's signed in to a canvas app.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/canvas-apps/show-current-user to sources for the explanation of whose details the User() defaults display.
